annotations.text: A BEAUTY BATH FOR "PINIONED"

Miss Abastenia St Leger Eberle ranks high among the women sculptors of America. Her latest work "Pinioned" was suggested to her while in Porto Rico- where she stood watching a seagull blow about by a tornado.

Miss Eberle has discovered that a bath of milk gives the figure a mellow tone that adds greatly to its attractiveness.

Giorgi's famous replica of the "Crouching Venus", a wonderful work of statuary, the original of which is gracing the Vatican gallery at Rome, bit of which four other's were made, by the wonderful sculptur of the fifteenth century, has been discovered and is now in Washington, in the house of Anthony R.Sanna, an engineer. It has been in the family for many years, but only recently discovered. When Mr. Sanna's father was in business in Italy, the statue was in his attic in a crate, but without his knowledge. When he moved to this country and established his business he intended leaving the old crate in Italy, but by mistake it was shipped, On the arrival of the crate it was stored away until recently, when it was opened accidentally. It happened that the Washington gallery of Art has a plaster cast of this statue and after Mr. Sanna, inquired he found that his statue was one of the four original statues made by the sculptor. He has been offered large sums of money for the piece of work, but refuses to part with it unless it be placed in a museum where he and the public can view it after it had been buried for so many senturies. 1/6/21

The Saint Gaudens status of Abraham Lincoln is the one which has been decided upon to stand in the Ganning inclosure at Westminster, London. The decision in favor of a duplicate of the Saint-Gaudens status in Chicago was announced this week in a report which Howard Russell Butler vice president of the National Academy of Design submitted to Herbert Adams president of the institution. The decision was made by King Georgi's First Commissioner of Works and in his report, Mr. Butler reported that the Gaudens Lincoln was the most suitable for erection in the chosen site of Westminster. The status was originally accepted in June 1913, to mark a century of Peace between Great Britain and the United States by the British Centenary Committee. In the spring of 1917, the chairman of the American PLACE Centenary Committee offered in place of the Gaudensstatue, a figure of Lincoln by George Grey Barnard stating that the latter figure was a superior substatute. The question then arose as to which of the two states was the most favorable and it was finally voted that the Gaudens statue was the most favorable. The above of the Saint-Gaudens status in Chicago is the one which will be reproduced to be sent to great Britain.

Among the latest accessions to the Metropolitan Museum of Art is an addition to its collection of Chinese sculpture, a large pottery figure of the Tang period, dating about $900 A.D. The figure is larger than life size, glazed in colors of the period green, white and yellow. It came from Ichou, southwest of Peking, where it was found in a cave of a mountain known as the Eight Lohan mountain. Ichans, one of which is represented in this sculpture were followers of Budha. S#368,787-88 Miss Irene McHugh,youthful sculptress of Tacoma, Wash., and photo of the plaster model of the bronze plaque presented to Commander Zachary Iansdowne of the U.S.S.Shenandoah upon the arrival of the great dirigible at Camp Lewis,Tacoma. The plaster cast was presented to Commander Iansdowne by Henry Sicade a full blooded Nisqually Indian and one of the oldest residents of Pierce County, Washington,who made the presentation speech, and the bronze will be delivered to the Sherandoah at Lakehurst soon.
The plaque portrays the Shenandoah approaching the Camp Lewis mooring mast,with a portion of the City of Tacoma in the foreground and Mt Tacoma( Rainier) looming up in the distance.

MRS, ALFRED GWYNE VANDERBILT, ONE OF
AMERICA'S MOST BEAUTIFUL WOMEN, IN MARBLE.

C. S. Pietro, known as "Society's Sculptor," has completed a marbles bust of Mrs. Alfred Gywnns Vanderbilt, considered one of the most beautiful women in America. It is on exhibition in the Gorham Galleries.

Art or critics pronounve the bust as the best marble portrait work Piotro has ever turned out. The Modeling is subtils, and has the air of exquisite refinement which is characteristic of Mrs. Vanderbilt's beauty.

Miss Yan McCleod, young New York sculptress, is seen at work on the idealistic head of Lloyd George which she will present to him, as a token of admiration for his policies, just before he returns to Europe.
Miss McLeod has idealized, in this work, the qualities of humanitarianism and reconciliation which she sees and admires in his international policies.

Among the swarm of "modernist" and "impressionist" works by sculptors who conceal their ignorance of anatomy by "new" technique--or lack of it--Miss McLeod has attracted attention by her fidelity to the eternal principles of human structure, The reason--she is the daughter of a surgeon and has studied her art in the dissecting room as much as in the atelier; like Michael Angelo she has started her sculpture with the scalpel.
